## ✨ Highlights

What v2026.11.17's lab campaign found, fixed: a member's move is
confirmed in seconds, a recycle that can't keep an address is refused
at once, and a cluster's Let's Encrypt orders its first certificates
right.

- ⏱️ **A move confirmed at its new address in 5 s** (was 34 s): a
  takeover or **Address** no longer waits on the address it leaves.
- 🔐 **A cluster's first HTTP-01 order succeeds**: every member answers
  with the ordering member's account before it orders.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Update the Controller and janusctl**: every fix is theirs (and the
  shared cluster engine). **Nothing changes on the nodes** - nodes on
  v2026.11.17 don't need this release.
- v2026.11.17's **Known issues** are the fixes below.

## 🧩 Clusters

- **A member's move confirmed at once at its new address**
  ([#663](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/663)): a takeover or
  **Address** waited about 34 s for nothing - the node applies its new
  configuration in milliseconds, its old address goes, and with it every
  message of the call made to that address, so the call waited for its
  30 s deadline before the old address was tried again. Now a call
  whose configuration drops its own address is let go 5 s after it
  left, and the confirmation tries the new address first - the
  Controller, `janusctl network apply` and `janusctl cluster` alike.
  - Measured: **34.2 s → 5.2 s** for the move of a recycled machine;
    on the lab, 5.1 to 5.7 s (was ~34 s) - a takeover of the member
    holding the virtual IP in 42 s (was 70 s), **Address** away and back
    in 16-18 s (was 45-47 s), no probe lost, never two VRRP masters.
  - When another interface of the configuration is on DHCP (it could
    take the address back), the call still waits for its deadline; the
    4 s on the old address are gone.
  - `janusctl network apply` no longer counts a call lost before
    "applying" as a failure when the node moved: it confirms.
  - A trial nothing could confirm - a configuration cutting the caller
    off - says **"couldn't confirm before …: the node went back to its
    previous configuration by itself"**, never "apply it again"
    ([#666](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/666)); "apply it
    again" is kept for a change that never reached the node. janusctl,
    the Controller and `janusctl cluster` alike.
- **A recycle or Address that can't keep the address is refused at once**
  ([#663](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/663)): a **409** with the
  reason, before any work and before a newcomer's machine is created -
  a cluster of one member, an address from DHCP, a cluster firewall
  depending on `.Member.Address`, a temporary address equal to the
  member's, a machine that can't be cloned. It was a 202, then an error
  from the background job, sometimes after a machine was created and
  destroyed again. On the lab: 409 in 6-19 ms, no machine created.
- **A cluster's first HTTP-01 order no longer races the others**
  ([#662](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/662)): when Let's
  Encrypt is set on the cluster, the other members learn the account
  of the member that orders - an imported key, the Controller's account
  when it orders, or that member's own, read from it first - before it
  may order. While its account isn't known, it is held as a follower
  (it orders nothing) and set free once the others answer for it. An
  unreadable account key is refused before anything changes. On the
  lab, v2026.11.17's failing case - no imported key, the challenge
  reaching the follower - got its certificates in 10 and 18 s, no
  Renew needed.
- **Renew orders at once with "Ordered by this Controller"**
  ([#662](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/662)): after a failed
  order, the cluster's **Renew** lifted nothing and the Controller
  tried again 5 to 10 minutes later; it now orders at once, like
  **Let's Encrypt › Order what's due now** - on the lab, issued 13 and
  21 s after Renew.
- **What an apply takes on or lets go is in the journal**
  ([#664](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/664)): an apply's
  `managed` list replaces the whole set - a domain left out stops being
  managed, its lock released on every member. An apply without `acme`
  stopped managing the cluster's Let's Encrypt with nothing in the
  journal; each domain taken on or let go is named there now, by the
  Controller and by `janusctl cluster apply -manage`
  ([Clusters](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#the-configuration)).

- `controller-libvirt-test` and `qemu-clusterctl-test` time a member's
  move (the libvirt test fails above 20 s); the cluster ACME tests order
  a first certificate validated on the follower, and Renew right after
  a refused order with the Controller ordering.
